title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth-Averaged Granular Avalanche Dynamics on Curved Topography
abstract: arXiv:2609.05542v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide a mesh-free framework for solving governing equations, but their application to granular avalanche dynamics over curved terrain remains largely unexplored. This study extends a depth-averaged PINN formulation based on the Savage-Hutter equations to an exponentially curved chute with spatially varying inclination and a strain-rate-dependent Mohr-Coulomb earth-pressure closure. The model is validated against measured front- and rear-edge trajectories from a laboratory granular-avalanche experiment, with selected observations withheld from training. A staged temporal curriculum proved essential for accurate prediction, reducing the held-out trajectory error by approximately two orders of magnitude compared with training over the full time domain from the outset. translated_title: 曲面地形上深度平均颗粒雪崩动力学的物理信息神经网络
translated_abstract: 物理信息神经网络（PINNs）为求解控制方程提供了一种无网格框架，但其在弯曲地形上颗粒雪崩动力学中的应用在很大程度上尚未被探索。本研究将基于Savage-Hutter方程的深度平均PINN公式扩展到一个具有空间变化倾角的指数弯曲溜槽，并采用了应变率相关的莫尔-库仑土压力闭合关系。该模型通过实验室颗粒雪崩实验中测量的前缘和后缘轨迹进行了验证，其中部分观测数据在训练中被保留（不参与训练）。分阶段的时间课程学习策略对准确预测至关重要，与从一开始就在整个时间域上进行训练相比，该策略将保留轨迹的预测误差降低了约两个数量级。稀疏数据实验进一步表明，在配置固定的情况下，观测点的位置比观测数量对结果的影响更大。
tldr: 本研究将基于Savage-Hutter方程的深度平均物理信息神经网络（PINN）扩展至指数弯曲溜槽上的颗粒雪崩动力学，证明分阶段时间课程学习可将保留观测的轨迹误差降低约两个数量级，且稀疏数据下观测点的位置比观测数量更为重要。
en_tdlr: This study extends a depth-averaged PINN formulation of the Savage-Hutter equations to granular avalanche dynamics on an exponentially curved chute, showing that a staged temporal curriculum reduces held-out trajectory errors by about two orders of magnitude and that observation placement matters more than observation number in sparse-data settings.
